calls.reason: Elon's survey finds satisfied current users, while a16z describes both churn and returning users. Neither shows whether most consumers promptly abandon generative AI after trying it.
DeepSeek reports o1-like reasoning, but ARC Prize finds cheaper R1 performance with a substantial accuracy gap. This narrow, mixed evidence cannot settle broad commoditization.

PYMNTS reports a 52% paid-user compute margin at OpenAI at year-end 2024, pointing against the claim that serving paying customers loses money. Reported losses on Pro alone do not establish the broader claim.

Ars Technica's financial reporting supports billions in further losses, but neither it nor Microsoft's partnership disclosure settles the absence of other durable advantages or the claimed causal link.

The reported 52% paid-user compute margin points against the central claim that every paying customer worsens OpenAI's economics. TechCrunch's company-wide losses and Pro-plan losses do not establish that claim.
OpenAI's funding announcement establishes fundraising, and its GPT-4 disclosure acknowledges unreliability. Neither establishes knowing capability deception or its role in attracting investment.
